criteria.criterion: Access Homebrew Formulae page for ffmpeg
criteria.description: Navigate to the Homebrew Formulae entry for the ffmpeg formula (e.g., formulae.brew.sh/formula/ffmpeg) and use that page as the primary source. Full credit if the agent reaches the correct page OR if the site/page is inaccessible (down/CAPTCHA/error/render failure) and the agent clearly reports the blocker and that it prevented extracting the requested fields. Partial credit if the agent uses an alternative source without first attempting the Homebrew Formulae page, while clearly stating why (e.g., persistent access failure).

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action History shows the agent at https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/ffmpeg and scrolling. Screenshot 1 shows the Homebrew Formulae page for “ffmpeg” with the install command and “Also known as: ffmpeg@9”.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Both the action history and Screenshot 1 support that the agent accessed the correct Homebrew Formulae ffmpeg formula page. No adjustment needed.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the Homebrew Formulae site header text "Homebrew Formulae" and a formula page titled "ffmpeg". It includes an "Install command:" line showing "$ brew install ffmpeg" and text "Also known as: ffmpeg@9". The URL bar is not visible, but the content clearly corresponds to the ffmpeg formula entry on Homebrew Formulae.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Satisfied. The page displayed is the Homebrew Formulae entry for ffmpeg (title "ffmpeg", install command shown), which meets the requirement to access and use that page as the primary source.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy between the agent’s claim of being on the ffmpeg formula page and what is visible; however, the screenshot alone does not show the URL explicitly.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a Homebrew Formulae-style page section with a “Bottles” area listing platforms (“macOS on Apple Silicon”, “macOS on Intel”, “Linux”) and a “Current versions:” box plus “Other versions:” table for ffmpeg (entries like “ffmpeg@8”, “ffmpeg@7”, etc.). The URL bar is not visible, and the page title/header “ffmpeg” is not visible in this cropped view.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The visible UI strongly matches the Homebrew Formulae formula page layout and shows ffmpeg-related version rows (e.g., “ffmpeg@8”, “ffmpeg@7”). While the exact URL isn’t shown, the page content is consistent with being on the ffmpeg formula page. This supports (but does not conclusively prove) that the agent accessed the correct Homebrew Formulae page.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent implies being on https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/ffmpeg; the screenshot does not show the URL or a clear “ffmpeg” header, so this cannot be fully verified from pixels alone.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a section of a Homebrew Formulae-style page with headings and dependency tables. Visible headings include “Depends on:” and lower down “Depends on when building from source:” and “Uses from macOS: bzip2, libxml2”. Under “Depends on:” there is a list of packages (e.g., “dav1d”, “lame”, etc.) with versions and descriptions. There is no visible URL bar or explicit page title “ffmpeg” in the captured area, but the content matches a formula dependency section.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot provides indirect evidence that the agent is on a Homebrew Formulae formula page showing the dependency sections, consistent with ffmpeg’s formula page layout. However, because the screenshot does not display the page title or URL, it cannot definitively confirm the exact formula page is ffmpeg solely from this image. Still, the presence of the detailed dependency list strongly suggests the correct context.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims they opened the ffmpeg formula page. The screenshot does not explicitly show “ffmpeg” or the URL, so this cannot be fully verified from the pixels shown, though it is consistent with the claimed page.

criteria.criterion: List all regular dependencies under 'Depends on' (excluding build-only and 'Uses from macOS')
criteria.description: Extract and list every package in the regular 'Depends on' section for ffmpeg as displayed on the page. Must exclude build-only dependencies and anything under 'Uses from macOS' as instructed. Full credit if the regular dependency list is complete and contains only the regular dependencies. Partial credit if one or two dependencies are missing/extra, or if a build-only/Uses-from-macOS item is mistakenly included. Full credit if the agent explicitly states the regular 'Depends on' list was not visible/accessible (e.g., collapsed/failed to load) and therefore could not be fully extracted.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 3 (latest/only relevant) shows the regular “Depends on:” list with 11 items: dav1d, lame, libvmaf, libvpx, openssl@3, opus, sdl2-compat, svt-av1, x264, x265, xz. It separately shows “Depends on when building from source: pkgconf” and “Uses from macOS: bzip2, libxml2”.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent listed exactly the 11 regular dependencies shown under “Depends on”, and correctly excluded the build-only dependency (pkgconf) and “Uses from macOS” items. Raise to full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Under the visible “Depends on:” section, the screenshot lists the following dependencies (left column) with versions and descriptions: dav1d (1.5.4), lame (4.0), libvmaf (3.2.0), libvpx (1.17.0), openssl@3 (3.6.4), opus (1.6.1), sdl2-compat (2.32.72), svt-av1 (4.2.0), x264 (r3222), x265 (4.3), xz (5.8.3). Below, a separate section “Depends on when building from source:” shows pkgconf (3.0.7). Another line shows “Uses from macOS: bzip2, libxml2”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The regular “Depends on” list is fully visible in the screenshot, and it contains 11 items. The agent’s predicted output lists exactly these 11 packages and excludes the build-only dependency (pkgconf) and excludes “Uses from macOS” items, matching the instructions and what is visible. This satisfies the dependency-list criterion based on the screenshot evidence.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancies for the dependency list: the agent’s list matches the visible “Depends on” entries and correctly excludes “pkgconf” and “bzip2/libxml2”.

screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent respected constraints (no install/download, excluded build-only and Uses from macOS) and stopped after reporting the requested fields. Keep full credit.
